quote: Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000. A per-transaction cap is close to illusory, so we have moved to the standard basis and confirmed that indemnification, confidentiality/data-security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 8, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. CORIO'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE SUBJECT TO THIS CAP.
ops.oldText: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.

proposal.summary: The cap is mutual, but it is limited to amounts "actually paid ... for the transaction which the liability relates to", which is far narrower than 12 months' fees and may be nominal; the only carve-out is Section 8, so confidentiality, data/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud all sit inside the cap. We move to 12 months' fees paid or payable (floor of USD 1,000,000) and add the standard Excluded Claims.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We must be able to assign to affiliates and to a successor without Vendor consent, and any residual consent right should be subject to a reasonableness standard.

ops.newText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; provided that Corio may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without consent to any of its affiliates or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.
ops.oldText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party.

proposal.summary: The M&A carve-out is helpful but there is no affiliate carve-out for us, the consent standard is unqualified, and consent is still required where our acquirer is a Commerce One competitor — which would give the Vendor a veto over our corporate transactions. We add an affiliate/successor carve-out and a reasonableness standard.

quote: Under no circumstances shall Commerce One contact Corio Customers regarding a non-ASP license sale, unless requested to do so by Corio.
rationale: All licences are non-exclusive and no sole-supplier or requirements obligation binds us; the only restraint runs against the Vendor in our favour, which is acceptable.
No liquidated damages, penalties or minimum termination payments are payable by us; the only refund mechanics run in our favour (Sections 3.1, 7.3 and 8.1).
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our licences must extend to affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf; the fallback is affiliate coverage on written notice.

proposal.summary: The licences are perpetual and irrevocable, which is good, but they run to Corio only — our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not covered, and the licence is limited to North America. We add affiliates and contractors to the internal-use grant.

quote: royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual right and license in the Territory to reproduce, install and use additional copies of the Software and Software tools and utilities
rationale: The licences are perpetual and irrevocable, which is good, but they run to Corio only — our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not covered, and the licence is limited to North America. We add affiliates and contractors to the internal-use grant.

quote: "CORIO MARKET SEGMENT" means those customers with annual sales revenues of less than $1,000,000,000.
rationale: Our sublicensing rights are confined to a customer revenue band and to North America, which operates as a field-of-use and territory restriction on the business we may write. If this reflects the intended commercial bargain we can live with it; otherwise we should widen the segment or secure the automatic worldwide expansion contemplated in Section 2.10 rather than a consent-based one.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit for five years with no exit. We have added a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund; if that is resisted we can move to 60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.newText: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement. In addition, Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.summary: There is a five-year committed term with termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency, and no convenience right for us. Our position is a Customer right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; the fallback is 60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Audits should be on 30 days' written notice (fallback 15 days), off-site and without access to our systems; the rest of this clause already meets our position.

ops.newText: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times during normal business hours and upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, and shall not include access to Corio's systems.
ops.oldText: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice.

proposal.summary: Frequency, auditor independence, cost allocation and the 5% shift are all acceptable; only the notice period is undefined. We fix it at 30 days' written notice during business hours and confirm no access to our systems.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA
rationale: California law with AAA arbitration and judgment enforcement in San Francisco falls within our accepted list; the seat is domestic, not foreign, so no change is required.
No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation is imposed on us anywhere in the Agreement or Exhibit B.

quote: subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer
rationale: The revenue-share is calculated on a deemed minimum of 40 users per Customer regardless of actual usage, and we commit to annual maintenance and MarketSite access fees for years 2–5 with no reduction right. Please confirm the commercial intent; our position is that fees track actual usage, with any commitment reducible on notice and trued up rather than penalised.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: Commerce One covenants that during the term of this Agreement, it will continue to require all Commerce One employees, agents, contractors or consultants to sign an Employee NDA/Invention Agreement
rationale: There is no non-solicitation or no-hire restriction binding us, so nothing to redline.

quote: this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration
rationale: Renewal terms are 12 months with a 30-day non-renewal window, which meets our preferred position; renewal pricing is fixed by Exhibit B rather than subject to uplift.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] On exit we need our data back in a usable format and reasonable transition help; our fallback is 90 days of assistance with data export within 30 days.

ops.newText: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers. In addition, upon expiry or termination for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Corio and Customer data in its possession in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.
